slides.title: Distribution channels
slides.text:
Distribution channels
Sets of interdependent organizations participating in the process of making a product or service available for use or consumption
American Marketing Association (AMA) describes channel as:
‘Structure of intra-company organization units and extra-company agents, dealers, wholesalers and retailers through which a product or service is marketed.’

slides.title: 2. Selecting Channel Members
slides.text:
2. Selecting Channel Members
Based on the number of channel intermediaries, three core distribution strategies:
Exclusive distribution
Intensive distribution
Selective distribution

bullets.text: Based on the number of channel intermediaries, three core distribution strategies:

slides.text:
Exclusive: Suppliers make agreements with one or few retailers, designating such retailers as the only ones to carry certain brands or products within a specified geographic area.
Intensive: Suppliers sell through as many retailers as possible (For convenience goods)
Selective: Suppliers sell through a moderate number of retailers (For shopping goods)

Types of power:
Coercive power- Threatening power in case of cooperation failure
Reward power- Benefits for performing specific acts

Expert power- Special knowledge that adds value to intermediaries
Referent power- Out of eminent position that the company holds in the industry

slides.title: Vertical Marketing Systems
slides.text:
Vertical Marketing Systems
A unified system of producer, wholesaler(s), and retailer(s)
Vertical Marketing System (VMS) is a collaboration between various distribution channel levels
Focuses on increasing efficiency and common shared goals
Benefits:
Minimizes channel conflicts
Increased efficiency

bullets.text: A unified system of producer, wholesaler(s), and retailer(s)
Vertical Marketing System (VMS) is a collaboration between various distribution channel levels
Focuses on increasing efficiency and common shared goals

slides.text:
Corporate vertical marketing system: In this, only one company is responsible for the whole production and distribution process. All the activities, including production, packaging, marketing, branding, etc., reside with one single company only. Eg. Zara, Reliance
Contractual vertical marketing system: An agreement between various intermediaries of the distribution chain. Under this system, an agreement stating the roles and responsibilities of each and every party is signed by all the parties of the distribution channel. Eg. McDonald’s
Administered vertical marketing system: Any one party of the distribution channel holds more power than the other parties of the distribution channel due to their size and market share.
